_note: Known things the gates cannot see. Printed on every run. This file exists because a limitation recorded in a README is prose, and prose gets forgotten — which is failure mechanism M4 in MANDATE.md. A blind spot that is not in output does not exist to the person reading output.

blindspots.limitation: SQL assembled into a variable on one line and executed on another is not detected.
blindspots.why: SQL patterns require an execution verb on the same line, to avoid flagging prose and log messages that merely contain the words DELETE FROM.
blindspots.closes_with: dataflow analysis, not a wider regex

blindspots.limitation: A call to a generic delete helper is invisible, because the call site contains no SQL.
blindspots.why: Found in fapp-claudedev/feeds/sqlite_adapter.py: a delete(table, filters) utility. A future caller would read `adapter.delete("matters", {...})` with no DELETE keyword anywhere on the line.
blindspots.closes_with: per-project declaration of project-specific deletion helpers, or call-graph analysis

blindspots.limitation: Outside Python, only provably empty catch blocks are detected.
blindspots.why: Python is analyzed with the AST and can distinguish a handler that logs from one that discards. Other languages fall back to a regex that can only recognise `catch {}` with certainty.

blindspots.limitation: A handler returning a meaningful default value is not flagged.
blindspots.why: Distinguishing a deliberate fallback from evasion requires reading intent, which is human judgment. Flagging every default would make the gate unusable.
blindspots.closes_with: nothing mechanical; this is a review question

blindspots.limitation: Documentation is never scanned. Markdown, text, and configuration prose pass through unexamined.
blindspots.why: The gates read source files only. PLAN.md, MANDATE.md and every other document in this repository have never been checked by anything.
blindspots.closes_with: a document gate, or an explicit decision that documents are out of scope

blindspots.limitation: Test code is excluded from every gate.
blindspots.why: Deferred-work markers, swallowed exceptions, and row removal are all normal in tests, and flagging them trains the reader to ignore output.
blindspots.closes_with: opt-in coverage for gates where test-code violations would matter

blindspots.limitation: Coverage is 6 of 200 software controls and 0 of 150 website controls. A clean run means only that three gates found nothing.
blindspots.why: Phase 1 is in progress. The remaining controls are PLANNED, ARTIFACT, HUMAN, or UNCLASSIFIED — see the coverage report.

blindspots.limitation: The software classification in controls/classification.json disagrees with docs/human-judgment-controls.md on how many controls need human judgment: 33 versus roughly 70.
blindspots.why: classification.json was derived from PLAN.md's gate-family table, which groups controls into families and takes the family's dominant type. human-judgment-controls.md was derived control by control and is finer-grained. The coarser reading is the optimistic one.
blindspots.closes_with: control-by-control reconciliation; until then the human count is a lower bound, not a figure
